description: Uses List/Dictionary-safe style correctly, but still uses generic syntax indirectly via arrays only; no issue there. Actual critical issue is elsewhere: the code creates runtime UI button instances in gameplay flow, which is not prohibited by itself, but the skeleton note explicitly says pre-created uiCanvas/guideText/scoreText should be used instead of creating new UI structures. More importantly, phase coverage is incomplete versus the validated 11-phase hospital/station management spec in the auto-promoted rules.

description: Mutates gameObject.name every frame/update-state with a large JSON string. In Luna this is risky and has caused instability/perf regressions; also bloated names can interfere with object lookup/debugging. While not explicitly banned, this is unsafe in a playable runtime.
fix: Expose state through a supported bridge/mechanism instead of renaming the GameObject every update, or update less frequently with constrained payload size.

description: Creates CTA button every frame after chargeStationState becomes 2? The guard is chargeStationState == 1, so button creation happens once at transition, but there is no protection against repeated CreateButton if state is reset or method re-entered unexpectedly. More importantly, it creates a new UI button instead of using the pre-mapped CTAButton pooled object / precreated UI pattern from skeleton guidance.
fix: Use a one-time creation guard and prefer skeleton-provided UI variables/patterns. If creating a button, ensure it is only created once with ctaBtn == null guard.

description: Calls GFM_UI.CreateText(...), which is an undocumented method. The rules explicitly say undocumented UI helpers like CreateText() may not exist and should be treated as compile-error risks.
fix: Replace CreateText() usage with only documented GFM_UI APIs, or implement guidance/UI through pooled scene objects instead.

description: The rule explicitly says the skeleton pre-creates uiCanvas, guideText, scoreText and they should be used directly instead of creating new ones. This script creates a new canvas and text objects in Start(). This is a documented production-risk violation.
fix: Use the pre-created uiCanvas, guideText, and scoreText references from the template; do not recreate the canvas/text in Start().

description: Input handling relies on Physics.Raycast against pooled objects, but the code never ensures those objects have colliders. In Luna pool setups, collider availability is not guaranteed, so clicks may never resolve to world positions and interaction can fail.
fix: Avoid dependence on physics raycasts for core interaction. Convert screen input to a ground-plane/world-plane position directly from camera math, or explicitly verify template-provided colliders exist before using raycasts.

description: Camera.backgroundColor is set to (0.45, 0.52, 0.62), which differs from ground color (0.75, 0.78, 0.82) by only 0.30, 0.26, 0.20. At least one RGB channel must differ by ≥ 0.3. Green and blue channels fail; red is exactly 0.30 and too borderline for production safety. Recommended deep sky blue was not used. This can trigger solid-color-screen detection.
fix: Use a safer background such as new Color(0.35f, 0.55f, 0.75f) or any color with at least one channel clearly >0.3 different from ground.

description: Camera initial positioning is wrong: camFollowOffset is set to (-7,10,-7), then camera position is set to new Vector3(-7,10,-1) + camFollowOffset, resulting in (-14,20,-8). This is far from the play area and likely misses the initial objects on first frame, risking a blank/solid-color screen despite objects being placed.
fix: Set the camera to Player position + camFollowOffset, e.g. after placing the player use mainCam.transform.position = Player.transform.position + camFollowOffset, and verify initial framing shows ground plus 3 colored objects.

description: Although three colored objects are placed in phase 1, there is no guaranteed assignment of the skeleton 'player' variable used by MovePlayer/IsNear/TryCollect/TryDeliver. As written, player remains null, so required interaction systems never work and later phases rely on auto-advance placeholders.
fix: Assign player = Player in Start() after finding pooled object, and implement actual interaction-driven phase logic.

description: The script creates a new canvas and new text objects with GFM_UI.CreateCanvas/CreateText even though the skeleton note explicitly says uiCanvas, guideText, and scoreText are pre-created and must be used directly instead of creating new UI structures. This is a documented production-risk violation.
fix: Remove runtime canvas/text creation and use the skeleton-provided uiCanvas, guideText, and scoreText references only.

More importantly, this adds an alternate CTA path outside the required GameEnded()->ShowCTA() end flow.

fix: Use the required game-end path only: call Luna.Unity.LifeCycle.GameEnded(); then ShowCTA(); If a visible CTA is needed, use skeleton-provided UI/CTA objects with a one-time guard instead of creating a new button at runtime.

description: Creates a new Canvas and new Text objects at runtime with `GFM_UI.CreateCanvas` and `GFM_UI.CreateText`, despite the rule that skeleton pre-creates `uiCanvas`, `guideText`, and `scoreText` and they should be used directly instead of creating new UI structures.
